questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university had some interesting courses and that my study destination was not so far away from my home-country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my study abroad experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and if I had any questions I just e-mailed the incoming exchange team/ international office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some questions about the courses I had to take, so I e-mailed the incoming exchange team and they helped me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. You could pay the university to get access to a webpage called ROOM. Here you could apply for student housing but you had to be quite fast at applying as it was a "first come - first served" principle. I lived at Uilenstede.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a kitchen that you share with approximately 12-14 other people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living at Uilenstede if you are a social and outgoing person who wants to live with other exchange students. Some of the best friends I made during the exchange were my flatmates. When you live with a lot of students the common areas can become dirty though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly can't remember right now but I remember it as being quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always contact the incoming exchange team/ international office and they were fast at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied for a minor in peace and conflict studies which included six different courses. It was easy to apply and I got all six courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a minor if you find a minor that you think sounds interesting. I personally liked that all the courses were to a certain degree intertwined and that I did not have to be worried about whether or not the courses would overlap in my schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were suitable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found the style of teaching a little bit different. I had exams every 2 months-ish as Vrije Universitet has a period system where a course is approximately 2 months. This made all the courses quite intense as you had to learn a lot within only two months.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Philosophy and the Ethics of Political Violence: Peace, War and Terrorism
- Political Violence and the Human Condition
- Conflict and Peacebuilding: Local and Global Perspectives 
- The Law and Politics of Fencing the Use of Force
- Peace and Conflict: From Theory to Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the whole minor. I really liked how all the courses were intertwined. My favorite course was "Political Violence and the Human Condition".

questions.answer: It was just as I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really explore any of the non-academic opportunities at my host institution but it seemed like there were a lot of things one could join if interested.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music, theater, debate clubs, etc... I did not attend any, so I do not know exactly what was available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I bought a museum-card. It costs 65 euros and can be used at 400 museums in the Netherlands.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Buy the museum card and use it to go to all the big museums like the Anne Frank museum, Van Gogh museum, Rijksmuseum etc. Take day trips to cities like Utrecht, Delft, Rotterdam, and Den Haag.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. Denmark and the Netherlands are really similar to each other and so are the people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live together with other students for example on a campus like Uilenstede. Use a lot of energy on socializing the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love how people bike everywhere just like in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First of all, go on exchange - you will not regret it. Secondly, get a bike as one of the first things. I bought one via Facebook Marketplace but a lot of people also rented one from Swapfiets. It is an easy way to get around when you have to go to uni but also when going into the city center. Last but not least, remember to enjoy it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I made during my exchange and also all the new knowledge I obtained during the courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think one of the greatest challenges was being away from my friends, family, and boyfriend back home. Luckily I met so many wonderful people on exchange!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a wonderful experience and I would definitely recommend it to everybody.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
